transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in today?

I guess… the main thing is I’ve gotten really slowed down, like physically slowed down. I work doing hair, and lately my hands just don’t do what they used to do. It feels like they’re moving through glue or something—like even simple stuff, sectioning someone’s hair cleanly, clipping it up, mixing color in the bowl, getting the brush ready… it all takes me forever now.

And it’s not just me being picky or careful. I used to be pretty quick with those things, like my hands kind of knew what to do automatically, and now I’m standing there thinking, “Why is this taking so long?” Clients and people at work have started noticing too, which is embarrassing. I’ll be halfway through something that should be quick and I can feel someone waiting on me, and it makes me more aware that I’m just… slower than I used to be.
Have you noticed yourself feeling down, losing interest in things you usually enjoy, or feeling like you’re not good enough lately?

Yeah… yeah, I have. It’s been most days, honestly. I’ll wake up and before anything even happens, there’s this heavy feeling in my chest, like this flat sadness just sitting there. It’s not even always like I’m crying or something dramatic, it’s more like… I open my eyes and it already feels like the day is too much, or like there’s no real point in trying to keep building the life I thought I was building.

I used to have these ideas about where I was going, with work and becoming better at hair and just having my own kind of life, and now when I think about it, it feels far away and kind of pointless. Like I’m not good enough to get there, or like even trying is stupid because I’m already behind somehow. It’s a really gross feeling because part of me knows I’m young and I’m supposed to be excited or motivated, but instead I just feel weighed down most mornings.
Have you noticed a loss of energy or felt unusually fatigued most days, even when you haven’t done much physically?

I’m not totally sure how to answer that, because I don’t know if I’d call it “tired” exactly. Like, I don’t feel like I ran a marathon or something. It’s more that everything takes so much more effort than it should, if that makes sense.

Some days I haven’t really done much yet, and I still feel like I’m dragging myself through the day, but I don’t always know if that’s energy or motivation or just me moving slower. I’ll be standing there thinking, “Why is this so hard to get started?” But I’m not sure if it’s physical fatigue in the way you mean. I guess I’ve noticed the dragging feeling more than, like, being sleepy or exhausted.
Have you found yourself feeling like you’re not good enough, or like you’re letting people down, even when there’s no clear reason for it?

Yeah… a lot. Probably more than I want to admit. I keep thinking I’m just this burden on everyone, like I’m making things harder for people who already have their own stuff to deal with.

It’s not even always tied to one clear thing happening that day. I’ll just start thinking about how I haven’t been able to keep my money together, or how work feels like it’s slipping, or how even basic salon responsibilities feel like too much sometimes, and then it turns into this whole thing in my head where I’m like, “Of course people are tired of me. Of course I’m disappointing everyone.”

And then there’s this other thought that feels really ugly to say out loud… like maybe I deserve what’s happening because I couldn’t keep basic parts of my life together. Like if I were more responsible, or more normal, or just better at handling things, I wouldn’t be in this position. I know that sounds harsh, but it feels true when I’m in it.
Have you had times in the past when you felt this way for two weeks or more, where these feelings weren’t just a passing mood but seemed to last day after day?

Yeah… this hasn’t really felt like a passing mood for a long time. I mean, if I’m being honest, the heavy depression feeling has been with me for about a year and two months now.

It’s not like every single minute is the exact same intensity, but it’s been there day after day in some form. Like even if I have a moment where I’m distracted or I’m laughing at something, underneath it there’s still that weight, and then it comes right back. So yeah, definitely more than two weeks. It’s been… a long stretch.

Before this current period of feeling down, have you ever had a time when you felt this way for at least two weeks, and then had a period of at least a couple of months where you felt back to normal before it came back again?

I’m not sure. I don’t really know how to separate it out cleanly like that, honestly.

Like, I can remember having rough patches before, but I don’t know if I could say for sure, “Yes, that was two full weeks, and then I was totally normal for two months.” My memory of it is more blurry than that. I think I’ve had times where I felt better, or where I was functioning more like myself, but I don’t know if I’d call it completely back to normal.

So… I don’t want to say yes if I’m not sure. I guess what I know is this current stretch feels different because it’s been so long and so constant. Before that, I don’t really have a clear timeline in my head.

Can you recall if there was ever a time before this current period where you felt this way for at least two weeks, and then later had a time where you felt clearly better and back to your usual self for at least a couple of months?

I’m really not sure. I’ve been trying to think about it when you ask, but I don’t want to give you an answer that sounds more certain than I actually feel.

Before this current stretch, I know I had periods where I wasn’t doing great, and then periods where I seemed more okay on the outside, like I could go to work or talk to people and not look like something was wrong. But whether I was actually back to my usual self for a couple months… I don’t know. That part is hard for me to say.

It’s like when I look back, everything kind of blends together. I can remember feelings and general phases, but not clean blocks of time like, “this was two weeks of depression” and then “this was two months of being normal.” I wish I could be more exact, but I just don’t remember it that clearly. So I guess my honest answer is I can’t really recall a definite time like that.
Have you ever had more than one time in your life when you felt this way for a while and then felt clearly better for several months before feeling down like this again?

I don’t think I can say that, no… not in a clear way.

Like, I’ve definitely had times in my life where I felt worse and then times where I seemed more okay, but “more than one time” with feeling this way for a while and then being clearly better for several months… I just don’t have that mapped out in my head. It’s not like I can look back and see separate episodes with clean breaks between them.

Some periods I was probably functioning better, and maybe people around me would’ve thought I was fine, but I don’t know if I actually felt clearly back to myself for several months. I’d be guessing if I said yes. So I guess the most honest answer is I’m not sure that’s ever happened in a way I can clearly remember.
Can you think back and recall if there was ever a time when you felt clearly better for at least two months between periods of feeling down like this?

I’m trying to think of it that way, but I really can’t pull out a clear example. Like, I know there were times where things felt less heavy, or I was doing more normal stuff and maybe seemed okay, but I don’t know if I could honestly say, “Yes, I was clearly better for two full months,” and then it came back.

It’s hard because when I look back, it doesn’t feel neatly divided. It’s more like there were ups and downs, and some stretches where I could get through the day better, but not necessarily like I was fully back to myself. So… I don’t think I can recall a definite two-month period like that between feeling down. I’m not saying it definitely never happened, I just don’t remember it clearly enough to say yes.
Can you recall if there was ever a time when you felt clearly better for at least two months between periods of feeling down like this?

I know I kind of answered this already, but… no, I still can’t really recall a clean period like that. I keep trying to go back through it in my head, like, “Was there a couple months where I was actually better?” and it just doesn’t come up clearly.

There were definitely times where I was more functional, like I could do regular things and probably didn’t seem as down from the outside. But feeling clearly better for at least two months, in between feeling this low… I don’t know. I don’t want to say yes just because there were lighter stretches. It feels more blurry than that, like it never separated into neat chunks for me.

So I guess my honest answer is I can’t remember a definite time where I was clearly better for two months between periods like this.
Have you ever had at least two separate times in your life when you felt this way for a while, and then had at least two months in between where you felt clearly better and back to your usual self?

I’m sorry, I know you’ve asked it a couple ways, and I’m not trying to be difficult. I just don’t think I can honestly say yes to that.

When you say “at least two separate times” and then “at least two months in between where I felt clearly better and back to my usual self,” that sounds really organized, like there were these distinct chapters where I was bad, then okay, then bad again. And when I look back, it doesn’t feel like that in my memory. It’s more blended together. There were times I was doing better than other times, definitely, and maybe I looked more normal or was keeping up with things more, but I don’t know that I felt clearly better and really back to myself for two months straight.

So… I don’t think I can identify two separate episodes like that. I can say there were ups and downs, but not clean breaks where I’d say, “Yes, that was two months of being back to my usual self before it came back.”

Can you think back and say for sure that you’ve had at least two separate times in your life when you felt this way for a while, and then had a time where you felt clearly better and back to your usual self for at least two months in between?

I don’t think I can say that for sure, no. Like, if you’re asking me to be definite about it, I can’t point to two separate times and then a clear two-month gap where I was really back to my usual self.

I keep trying to sort it in my head, but it doesn’t feel that clean. There were periods where I was probably doing better, or I could get through things more normally, and maybe from the outside it looked like I was okay. But “clearly better” and “back to myself” for at least two months… I can’t honestly say I remember that happening between episodes.

So I guess my answer is no, not for sure. I’m not saying my mood was exactly the same every single day, because it wasn’t, but I can’t identify that kind of definite break you’re asking about.

Can you recall if there was ever a time before this current period when you had a clear improvement in your mood, where you felt noticeably better for several months and were able to function normally in your daily life?

I think… looking back, before now, it mostly feels like this whole decline has been me feeling depressed and weighed down most of the time. Not necessarily every second of every day, but the overall pattern was that heaviness was kind of there more often than not.

There were shorter stretches where the sadness wasn’t as loud, I guess. Like I could get through my day more normally, or I wasn’t thinking about how bad I felt every minute, and I might have seemed more okay. But I don’t know that I’d call it a clear improvement for several months where I was functioning normally and really felt like myself again.

It feels more like brief lighter periods inside something that was still mostly low, if that makes sense. So no, I can’t really recall a clear several-month period before this where I was noticeably better in a full way.

Looking back over your life, can you think of a time before this current period when you had a stretch of at least two months where you felt clearly better, back to your usual self, and were functioning normally in your daily life?

I’m trying to think of it honestly, and… I don’t think I can give you a clear yes to that.

Like, there were definitely times where I seemed more functional, I guess. I could go to work or get through normal daily stuff better than at other times, and maybe if someone saw me then they would think I was doing okay. But when you say “clearly better” and “back to my usual self” for at least two months, that’s where I get stuck, because I don’t really remember a stretch that clean.

It’s more like there were easier patches, but I still didn’t feel fully like myself. I don’t want to exaggerate and say it was a full recovery period if it wasn’t. So… no, I can’t really think of a time before this where I had at least two months of feeling clearly back to normal and functioning normally.
